correctness.rationale: For two agents with independent identical-in-law utility rows, ex-post EF probability equals p(1-p). Exponential Laplace transforms give exact singleton and pair formulas. The three-item proof compares all splits by monotonicity; for the four-mean family singleton and pair classes each have a unique best split; rational factorization yields an exact cubic sign threshold. The general a<b asymptotic follows from expansion of the same rational formulas. Exact standard-library checker covers 2,427 finite split comparisons but is not substituted for the analytic infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the exact minimal good count for independent heterogeneous exponential valuations, an all-real-parameter cubic optimizer switch, and a robust continuum of reversals. Prior published work proves convolution-power optimality and general log-concave approximation with a four-good counterexample outside the all-exponential class; a recovered prior pair-ordering result compares only 2+2 splits. No claim of general four-item counterexample originality is made.

value.rationale: Expected-value EF and maximum realized EF probability are distinct allocative policies. A smallest-good boundary, exact rational counterexample, explicit phase transition, and robustness for every pair of unequal smaller means together identify a natural stable statistical mechanism, rather than an arbitrary isolated finite calculation. The positive gap can be small near threshold, but the classification and structural failure apply to a continuum of exponential models.
